name: Question 7
problem: The curve $C$ is the intersection of a surface $S,$ defined by $z=f(x,y),$ with the plane $x=0.5.$ Given that the point $P(0.5,2,4)$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{y}=y+2y\operatorname{ln}⁡(xy)+\frac{1}{x}$, find the equations of the tangent line to $C$ at $P.$
worked_solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface $z=f(x,y)$ with the plane $x=0.5.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $P(0.5,2,4)$ will be given by the partial derivative $\frac{∂z}{∂y}{|}_{(0.5,2)}.$ 

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative $\frac{∂z}{∂y}$ at $(0.5,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂y}{|}_{(0.5,2)} & =2+2(2)\operatorname{ln}⁡((0.5)(2))+\frac{1}{0.5} \\  & =2+4\operatorname{ln}⁡1+2 \\  & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line: 

$$
\begin{aligned}z-z{|}_{(0.5,2)} & =\frac{∂z}{∂y}{|}_{(0.5,2)}(y-2) \\ z-4 & =4(y-2) \\ z & =4y-4\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the curve $C$ at $P(0.5,2,4)$ can be given as the intersection of two planes, as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}x=0.5 \\ z=4y-4\end{aligned}
$$

a
{x=0.5z=−4y+12
b
{x=0.5z=4x+2
c
{x=0.5z=4y−4
d
{y=2z=4x+2
e
{x=0.5z=4y−12

Correct
EXPLANATION

The curve C is the intersection of the surface z=f(x,y) with the plane x=0.5. Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point P(0.5,2,4) will be given by the partial derivative ∂z∂y|(0.5,2).

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative ∂z∂y at (0.5,2):

∂z∂y|(0.5,2)=2+2(2)ln⁡((0.5)(2))+10.5=2+4ln⁡1+2=4

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

z−z|(0.5,2)=∂z∂y|(0.5,2)(y−2)z−4=4(y−2)z=4y−4
